_note: 30-card starter deck (12 quiz, 9 choice, 9 event). Effects: money in £M, gp, meter change applied immediately. Facts checked Nov 2026; NISRA/DfE figures update yearly.

cards.text: What year does Northern Ireland's Climate Change Act set as the deadline for net zero?
cards.fact: The Climate Change Act (Northern Ireland) 2022 sets a target of net zero emissions by 2050.

cards.text: By 2030, Northern Ireland's emissions must be at least how much lower than the baseline?
cards.fact: The Act's 2030 interim target is a cut of at least 48%. That's the game's 2030 checkpoint.

cards.text: Which sector produces the most greenhouse gases in Northern Ireland?
cards.fact: Agriculture produced 31.4% of Northern Ireland's emissions in 2024, the largest share of any sector.

cards.text: In 2025, about how much of Northern Ireland's electricity came from renewable sources?
cards.fact: 47% of electricity came from renewables in the year to December 2025. The target is at least 80% by 2030.

cards.text: Which source makes most of Northern Ireland's renewable electricity?
cards.fact: Wind provided 72% of Northern Ireland's renewable electricity in 2025.

cards.text: What is the most common main heating in Northern Ireland homes?
cards.fact: 61% of households used oil central heating as their main heating in 2024/25, down from 70% in 2015/16.

cards.text: Roughly how much of Northern Ireland's land is peatland?
cards.fact: Peatland covers about 18% of Northern Ireland, around 242,600 hectares.

cards.text: Why are damaged peat bogs bad for the climate?
answers: They release carbon they have stored
cards.fact: About 80% of Northern Ireland's peatlands are damaged and releasing carbon. Healthy peat stores about 45 years' worth of NI's current emissions.

cards.text: Lough Neagh supplies about how much of Northern Ireland's drinking water?
cards.fact: About 40%. In 2023 a huge algae bloom spread across the lough after record warm water and excess nutrients from farming and wastewater.

cards.text: What is Northern Ireland's highest recorded temperature?
cards.fact: 31.3°C at Castlederg, Co Tyrone, on 21 July 2021.

cards.text: As well as being a park and cycle path, what does East Belfast's Connswater Community Greenway do?
cards.fact: The 9 km greenway follows three rivers and was completed in 2017. Its flood defences protect about 1,700 properties.

cards.text: In 2013, Belfast Harbour opened the first purpose-built facility in the UK or Ireland for what?
cards.fact: The £50m D1 terminal is used to assemble offshore wind turbines.

cards.text: A gas supplier offers your businesses a cheap long-term contract.

options.label: Retrofit your offices to use less energy

cards.fact: Northern Ireland must get at least 80% of its electricity from renewables by 2030.

cards.text: An airline will add new routes from Belfast if you invest.

options.label: Fund a public transport link to the airport instead

cards.fact: Transport produced 21.3% of Northern Ireland's emissions in 2024.

cards.text: The old boilers in your buildings need replacing.
cards.fact: 61% of Northern Ireland households still rely on oil as their main heating.

cards.text: A developer wants to drain a peat bog you look after to build warehouses.
cards.fact: About 80% of Northern Ireland's peatlands are damaged and releasing carbon. Restoring them locks it back in.

cards.text: Farmers ask you to back a big intensive livestock expansion near Lough Neagh.

options.label: Fund buffer strips and better slurry storage instead

cards.fact: Agriculture is Northern Ireland's biggest source of emissions (31.4% in 2024), and farm nutrients helped feed the 2023 Lough Neagh algae bloom.

cards.text: The council asks what should go on a city-centre site you own.

options.label: Protected cycle lanes and a Glider stop

cards.fact: Belfast's Glider buses started in September 2018, linking East and West Belfast through the city centre.

cards.text: A new data centre you're backing needs a power supply.

options.label: Pay extra for a renewable contract

cards.fact: 47% of Northern Ireland's electricity came from renewables in 2025.

cards.text: The 2030 target is close, and the council asks everyone to cut emissions now.
cards.fact: Targets have deadlines along the way: Northern Ireland must cut emissions by at least 48% by 2030, not just reach net zero by 2050.

cards.text: A developer wants to build homes on a floodplain beside the River Lagan.
cards.fact: Nature-based defences work: the Connswater Community Greenway protects about 1,700 East Belfast properties from flooding.

cards.text: A red wind warning! Storms bring down power lines across your properties.
cards.fact: Storm Éowyn brought a rare red wind warning to Northern Ireland in January 2025, and about 285,000 customers lost power.

cards.text: A record heatwave pushes up cooling costs for your buildings.
cards.fact: Northern Ireland's record temperature is 31.3°C, set at Castlederg on 21 July 2021.

cards.text: You win a contract supplying the new offshore wind industry.
cards.fact: Northern Ireland plans to start generating offshore renewable energy in its waters from 2030.

cards.text: An algae bloom on Lough Neagh hits businesses you've invested in.
cards.fact: Lough Neagh supplies about 40% of Northern Ireland's drinking water. Its 2023 bloom followed record water temperatures of 21°C.

cards.text: The council launches a green investment grant.
cards.fact: Belfast City Council declared a climate emergency in 2019.

cards.text: Roadworks for a new Glider route disrupt your businesses.
cards.fact: The Glider's two routes link East and West Belfast and the city centre with the Titanic Quarter.

cards.text: A very windy month brings cheap electricity.
cards.fact: Wind makes 72% of Northern Ireland's renewable electricity.

cards.text: New emissions figures are published, and investors reward early movers.
cards.fact: Northern Ireland's net emissions fell 29.4% between the 1990 baseline and 2024, from 26.0 to 18.4 million tonnes of CO₂e.

cards.text: Your draughty buildings run up big winter heating bills.
cards.fact: Buildings (homes, public and commercial) produced 15.5% of Northern Ireland's emissions in 2024.
